title: Docker published ports and host bindings
text: Compose ports without an explicit host IP bind to all host addresses by default. Bind local research services to 127.0.0.1. A published Redis, PostgreSQL, Nginx or MinIO port is potential exposure; actual reachability depends on networking and vantage. Internal exposure is not automatically a policy violation.

title: Redis protected mode and access control
text: Redis is intended for trusted clients in trusted environments. Restrict network access and configure authentication. Disabling protected-mode removes a protective mechanism; inspect network boundaries and ACLs before concluding that unauthenticated access is possible.

title: PostgreSQL trust authentication
text: PostgreSQL trust authentication permits connecting clients to claim a database user without a password. Treat POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD trust or a matching pg_hba host trust rule as a candidate weak-authentication finding. TCP reachability alone does not prove a database login succeeds.

title: Kubernetes RBAC least privilege
text: Grant Kubernetes RBAC permissions narrowly. Wildcard verbs resources or apiGroups may grant unintended permissions, including future resource types. A Role or ClusterRole must also be examined with its bindings to determine effective access.

title: Kubernetes secret handling
text: Kubernetes Secret data is encoded, not made confidential by base64. Avoid committing literal passwords, tokens and secret values to deployment artifacts. Prefer external secret provisioning and controlled references. A reference valueFrom secretKeyRef is not itself a leaked secret.

title: Kubernetes privileged containers
text: Privileged containers bypass important isolation controls. The Baseline pod security policy disallows privileged containers, including init and ephemeral containers. Explicit privileged true requires investigation.

title: Kubernetes service exposure types
text: NodePort publishes service ports on nodes and LoadBalancer requests an external load balancer. ClusterIP is cluster internal by default. These types indicate intended exposure, not proof of public Internet reachability or a vulnerability.

title: AWS security group ingress rules
text: An ingress CIDR of 0.0.0.0/0 permits all IPv4 sources and ::/0 permits all IPv6 sources for the specified traffic. Reachability also depends on routing, addresses, network ACLs and listening services. Terraform security group configuration alone does not prove access.

title: Nginx directory indexing
text: The Nginx autoindex module generates directory listings. The autoindex directive defaults to off. Explicit autoindex on may reveal directory contents when no index file is available; whether this violates policy depends on the intended content.
